problem: Prior spatial-cognition benchmarks for VLMs (e.g. Theory of Space) study curiosity-driven exploration but not safety-critical, goal-driven settings. It is unclear whether VLM decisions rest on physical evidence or on textual priors, and whether VLM memory resembles human memory.
motivation: VLMs are being considered for safety-critical tasks such as emergency evacuation, where hallucination, prior override, visual degradation and forgetting can be dangerous. The paper asks whether VLM spatial maps, memory and evacuation choices are reliable and grounded under partial observability and hazards.
key_idea: Extend Theory of Space into an Explore-Map-Remember-Decide (EMRD) pipeline with new coverage, positional, psychological-memory and focal-point grounding metrics, and test 7 VLMs in an AI2-THOR office evacuation task.
insight: Inter-model or inter-start consensus on the evacuation room can hide a lack of spatial grounding. Qwen3-VL-32B still picks the Conference Room 68.4% of the time with anonymised room labels, and removing the prompt object inventory drops that preference from 88.6% to 27.5%, so the choice depends on the prompt inventory and pretrained priors, with exploration serving as post-hoc justification. Low light degrades coverage and map stability while texture/colour randomisation barely matters. Memory does not follow the human U-shaped serial-position curve or the 7±2 capacity limit (GPT-5.4 holds ~40-50 objects, InternVL3-14B ~5-10).
method: Scenario: a ProcTHOR/AI2-THOR 4-room office (Entrance, Office, Conference, Kitchen), first-person RGB, discrete Goto/Turn/Term(r) actions, 50-step budget, formalised as a POMDP; the agent keeps a JSON cognitive map with a deduplication check.
Explore metrics: Absolute Environment Coverage (capped per-type matched instances / GT inventory) and Temporal Efficiency (mean step count).
Map metrics: Procrustes-aligned Positional Accuracy and Temporal Belief Stability (drift weighted by map coverage, anchored to the baseline object count).

Remember metrics: Ebbinghaus exponential forgetting with censored MLE and R² vs Kaplan-Meier, serial-position TTF by Early/Middle/Late discovery bins, and Miller's-law forgetting probability vs map size.
Decide metrics: focal-point agreement across start rooms, plus Focal-Point Spatial Grounding (global and local) and unvisited-room rate.

Stress tests and interventions: low light/visibility (~50% reduction) and texture/colour randomisation; on Qwen3-VL-32B, equalised room descriptions, anonymous room labels and an inventory-free prompt, tested with χ² and Fisher tests.

setting.backbone: Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.8 (frozen); Qwen3-VL-32B, Ovis2-34B, Pixtral-12B, InternVL3-14B (frozen, prompted)
setting.observation: egocentric first-person RGB plus topological/movement feedback
setting.action_space: discrete semantic actions Goto(target), Turn(angle), Term(room)
setting.privileged: room names and object inventory given in the prompt; perfect odometry; GT used only for evaluation

numbers_note: Custom EMRD evaluation, not a standard navigation benchmark. Results are AEC/TE, FPSG and memory metrics, so they are not listed under canonical benchmarks.
results: Only Gemini-3.1-Pro and Claude Opus 4.8 nearly always visit their chosen room (never visited ≤7.5%); Pixtral-12B picks an unvisited room in 47.9% of episodes. Gemini-3.1-Pro has the highest coverage (59.4% AEC baseline), and FPSG_glob is low everywhere (0.096-0.338). Low light lowers coverage by up to ~10 points, texture changes have little effect, and only 5 of 7 models fit exponential forgetting (R²≥0.65).
limitations: Single office layout, static hazards and one safety prompt
Prompt includes a text-biased object inventory; perfect odometry and discrete actions isolate mapping but are unrealistic
Interventions run only on Qwen3-VL-32B; 80 runs per condition
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
